title_en: The one who was dead and was given life and light
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The one who was dead and was given life

claims.statement_en: The ayah asks whether one who was dead, and whom God gave life and made for him a light by which he walks among people, is like one whose similitude is in the darknesses, from which he does not come out.
The ayah says that thus what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah asks whether one who was dead and whom God gave life and made a light for, by which he walks among people, is like one whose similitude is in the darknesses [c1]. It adds that what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah asks a question [c1]. It asks whether one who was dead, and whom God gave life and made for him a light by which he walks among people, is like one whose similitude is in the darknesses, from which he does not come out [c1]. The ayah says that thus what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah is a question, and it sets states side by side: given life and light, and darknesses from which there is no coming out [c1]. The first person walks among people by the light, and the ayah uses the word for a similitude (mathal) of the one in the darknesses [c1]. The ayah closes by saying what was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The ayah asks about one who was dead and whom God gave life and a light to walk among people by [c1]. It asks whether he is like one who is in the darknesses and does not come out [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah sets life and light beside darknesses from which there is no coming out [c1]. Another reading is that the ayah ends by saying that what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the one who was dead and the one in the darknesses are; the ayah names no one.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later commentary names the persons it takes them to be; this draft does not repeat or vouch for them.
- Not established: whether dead is meant of the body or of the state of belief; this draft keeps the ayah's word and leaves the sense open.
- The ayah uses the word for a similitude (mathal) of the one in the darknesses, and puts the whole as a question.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to this ayah.
The sense of mayyitan (dead) and the grammar of the question in 6:122 are for a scholar to decide.
